title: Australia event revenue estimate: supported limitations

claims.text: Monetary basis: all estimates are expressed in constant 2025 USD, GDP-deflated, at a fixed 2025 exchange rate. Because the price and exchange-rate response to the event is not modeled, results do not capture event-induced inflation or currency-movement effects on nominal revenue.

Scope: the estimate is a conditional scenario difference, defined as government revenue without the event minus revenue with the event, conditioned on the stated macroeconomic path. It is not a causal attribution, not a total-economy loss, and not a sovereign default probability.

Sectoral scope: the transmission channel modeled is agriculture, forestry and fishing value added feeding into conditional government revenue. Revenue figures include grants. Non-agricultural growth is proxied by IMF total real GDP growth shared across cases, which limits the representation of non-agricultural event effects.

Validation limitation: the fiscal model was validated via conditional holdout with realized inputs on latest revised history, and rolling-hindcast comparisons used a conditional final-vintage ridge challenger. These are conditional checks, not direct validation of Bayesian posterior forecasts, and passing convergence diagnostics alone does not establish predictive skill.

Provenance limitation: the assessment manifest marks historical input provenance as incomplete and the bundle as inspection-only, not recomputable; the underlying modeling does not claim causal identification.

Climate-conditioning limitation: official forecasts provide marginal rather than joint distributions, and the time-series extension used to fill the joint path is not itself a NOAA forecast; residual cross-country dependence is captured only through shared-year residuals.

limitations: The fixed evidence packet is bounded; absent quantiles or scenario parameter values cannot be retrieved or recomputed, so distributional detail beyond the reported mean, loss probability and expected shortfall is unavailable.
All figures are model outputs conditional on the stated macroeconomic path and the forecast vintage; they are scenario differences and associations, not causal estimates.
Australia estimates are single-country values; they must not be summed with other countries' quantiles, and aggregate scopes in the packet are not substitutes for the Australia-specific cell.
The signed mean keeps gains and losses, while the expected shortfall applies only to the positive part of the loss distribution; the two measures are not directly comparable.
Historical input provenance is incomplete and the bundle is marked for inspection only, so independent recomputation of the estimates is not supported.
Price and exchange-rate responses to the event are not modeled; values are in constant 2025 USD at a fixed 2025 exchange rate, so nominal revenue effects are out of scope.
